prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. ONE SQUARE memory-card PNG, an expert maritime illustrator's finished coloured-pencil, graphite and restrained watercolour sketch.
Reference is STYLE AND FRAMING ONLY: match the Titanic image's fine pencil strokes, hatching, paper highlights, soft upper-left light and ivory paper. Draw the NEW ship below.
CRITICAL LAYOUT: SMALL CENTRED subject on a big blank square page. Whole vessel fits in the CENTRAL 60% of width AND height. Leave broad empty ivory paper: about ONE FIFTH of the page on each of the four sides. Include every mast, bowsprit, sail and stern. Do not fill the page. No border.
One complete upright vessel as an above-water waterline portrait, intact in working heyday. Neat waterline edge, no visible underwater keel. Entire background is the same subtle warm ivory drawing paper edge to edge. NO text, letters, numbers, logos, captions, flags, signature or watermark; NO water, ocean, sky, horizon, scenery, wake, smoke, shadows, people or other vessels. Detailed natural colours and recognisable geometry, visibly hand drawn, not photo, CGI, toy, cartoon or vector.
Subject and view: HMB Endeavour. Cook's eighteenth-century collier-built exploration bark, broad rounded bluff bow, THREE wooden masts, cream square sails with rigging, warm brown stocky hull, deep blue topside panel and ochre trim, small raised quarterdeck. Clearly broad-bodied and practical rather than sleek clipper. View: port quarter; stern lower right, bow upper left. Keep the whole vessel upright, centred and within the central 68% of BOTH dimensions, generous blank paper on every side.
MATCH THE REFERENCE'S MODEST OBJECT SIZE. The new vessel is a small sketch surrounded by abundant unmarked ivory paper, its longest dimension is only about half of the square. Treat the reference's blank margins as locked.
review: Full-size visually reviewed; complete silhouette, recognisable major rig/turrets and safe margins.
